chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:

I asked him about garments made in al-Basrah in the manner of Yemeni woven cloth, from silk and cotton: is it suitable for the dead to be shrouded in it? He said: "If the cotton is more than the silk, then there is no harm."

key_terms.الْبَصْرَةِ: al-Basrah, the place where the cloth was manufactured
key_terms.الْعَصْبِ الْيَمَانِيِّ: Yemeni-style woven cloth used as a point of comparison for the fabric
key_terms.ثِيَابٍ: garments or cloths being asked about for use as a shroud
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection or legal problem
key_terms.يُكَفَّنَ: to be used for shrouding the deceased

ai.seo_question: Can the deceased be shrouded in a cloth made of both silk and cotton?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about shrouding the deceased in a fabric blended from silk and cotton. It permits using such cloth for the dead when the cotton content is greater than the silk, indicating a material-based legal distinction in funerary preparation.
